title: Decidability of zeros in integer linear recurrences
decision_reason: Source-matched formulation, independent September status, full scope comparisons, separate A28 self-pass and local validation passed; no matching unresolved general-resolution claim located.

problem_fingerprint.dimension: Arbitrary finite order d≥1, part of the input.
problem_fingerprint.domain: Index n∈N_0; values and input coefficients in Z.
problem_fingerprint.regularity_and_data_class: All integer initial values and coefficients with c_d≠0; repeated roots permitted.
problem_fingerprint.parameter_range: No fixed upper bound on order, coefficient size or time index.
problem_fingerprint.quantifiers: One algorithm must halt with the correct zero-existence answer for every finite input.
problem_fingerprint.limit_regime_and_order: Unbounded existential natural-number index; no asymptotic approximation.
problem_fingerprint.requested_conclusion: Determine whether the decision problem is decidable.
problem_fingerprint.computational_model_and_dependencies: Finite binary integer input; ordinary effective algorithm, no runtime constraint and no number-theoretic conjectural assumptions.

statement_source_and_scope_match: SUR26 Problem 2 uses nonsingular rational recurrences and explicitly reduces rational input to integer input preserving zeros. DS26 §1 independently gives the c_d≠0 integer convention and open status. BAC26 Problem 0 supplies current explicit formulation.
proposed_statement_text: Does an algorithm always halt and decide whether an arbitrary nonsingular integer linear recurrence, specified by its coefficients and initial values, has a zero at a nonnegative integer index?
applied_significance: Exact hyperplane reachability for discrete linear systems and termination from a specified state of a loop guarded by a linear disequality; foundational verification rather than numerical linear algebra.

closest_existing_or_new_entries.distinction: Real-time c^T exp(tA)x_0=0 for rational ODE data, versus natural-number powers and integer recurrence zeros.
Polynomial-time finite-circuit identity decision, versus existence of any halting procedure for an unbounded recurrence index.

DSSEP26 §1.3 provides a second, September 2026 assessment by the same independent author pair; it is not counted as a third independent team.
strongest_known_partial_results_and_gap: Unconditional order≤4; bounded-horizon fixed-order algorithms and restricted root classes. Simple recurrences have conditional algorithms; July 2026 gives conditional general decidability and an unconditional density-one universal set. No general unconditional algorithm or undecidability result located.
